📊 Grade Comparison: Completed vs. Not Completed (per Module)

Comprehensive Documentation

🎯 Overview

This feature performs statistical analysis comparing student grades between those who completed specific support modules versus those who did not. It uses both parametric and non-parametric statistical tests to determine if module completion has a significant association with academic performance.

Key Question Answered: Do students who complete optional support modules perform better in their reflections compared to students who don't complete these modules?

📁 Data Sources & Structure

1. Student Reflection Data

Source: course.students[email].reflection_data[reflection_num]
Structure:
student.reflection_data = { 1: {'reflection': Reflection_obj, 'grades': {'Current Score': 85.5, ...}}, 2: {'reflection': Reflection_obj, 'grades': {'Current Score': 78.2, ...}}, 3: {'reflection': Reflection_obj, 'grades': {'Current Score': 92.1, ...}}, 4: {'reflection': Reflection_obj, 'grades': {'Current Score': 88.7, ...}} }

2. Module Completion Data

Source: student.reflection_data[*].grades (across all reflections)
Identification: Columns containing 'feedback quiz' (case-insensitive)
Completion Criteria: Score > 0
# Example grade columns that indicate module completion: { 'Personal Finance Feedback Quiz': 5.0, # ✅ Completed (score > 0) 'Resume Writing Feedback Quiz': 0.0, # ❌ Not completed 'Interview Skills Feedback Quiz': 3.5, # ✅ Completed 'Group Work Module Feedback Quiz': 2.0 # ✅ Completed }

3. Grade Extraction Logic

# From grade_module_correlation_helper.py lines 1132-1157 for student in course.students.values(): # Extract reflection grade (default: Reflection 4) grade = None grades_dict = student.reflection_data.get(reflection_num, {}).get('grades') if grades_dict and 'Current Score' in grades_dict: try: grade = float(grades_dict['Current Score']) except Exception: grade = None # Extract completed modules across ALL reflections completed_modules = set() for ref in student.reflection_data.values(): grades = ref.get('grades', {}) for col, val in grades.items(): if 'feedback quiz' in col.lower(): try: if float(val) > 0: # Completion criterion completed_modules.add(col.strip()) except Exception: continue

🔄 Analysis Workflow

Step 1: Data Extraction
  • Iterate through all students in the course
  • Extract Reflection 4 grade (the 'Current Score' field)
  • Scan all reflections for feedback quiz columns
  • Determine module completion status (score > 0)
Step 2: Data Preprocessing
  • Create DataFrame with student data
  • Remove students with missing grades
  • Apply outlier removal if specified (IQR or threshold method)
  • Generate module completion summary statistics
Step 3: Statistical Analysis (Per Module)
  • Split students into two groups: completed vs. not completed
  • Perform normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk)
  • Execute Mann-Whitney U test (non-parametric)
  • Execute Welch's t-test (parametric)
  • Determine recommended test based on normality
Step 4: Visualization & Export
  • Generate box plots comparing grade distributions
  • Create summary tables with statistical results
  • Export raw data and results to CSV files
  • Apply color coding for statistical significance

📊 Statistical Methods Used

1. Mann-Whitney U Test (Primary)

scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu(group1, group2, alternative='two-sided')
  • Type: Non-parametric test
  • Purpose: Compare distributions between two independent groups
  • Assumptions: Independent observations, ordinal or continuous data
  • Null Hypothesis: The two groups have identical distributions
  • Alternative: One group tends to have higher/lower values

2. Welch's T-Test (Secondary)

scipy.stats.ttest_ind(group1, group2, equal_var=False)
  • Type: Parametric test
  • Purpose: Compare means between two independent groups
  • Assumptions: Normal distributions, independent observations
  • Advantage: More robust than Student's t-test (handles unequal variances)
  • Null Hypothesis: The means of the two groups are equal

3. Shapiro-Wilk Normality Test

scipy.stats.shapiro(data)
  • Purpose: Test if data follows a normal distribution
  • Null Hypothesis: Data is normally distributed
  • Decision Rule: p < 0.05 suggests non-normal data
  • Usage: Determines which test (parametric vs. non-parametric) to recommend

🎨 Visualization Components

1. Module Completion Summary Table

  • Columns: Module, Students Completed, Total Students, Completion Rate (%)
  • Color Coding:
    • ≥75% - High completion (green)
    • 50-74% - Medium completion (yellow)
    • 25-49% - Low completion (light red)
    • <25% - Very low completion (red)

2. Statistical Results Table

  • Descriptive Stats: N, Mean, Median for each group
  • Test Results: U-statistic, p-values, t-statistic
  • Normality Tests: Shapiro-Wilk p-values for both groups
  • Recommendations: Which test to trust based on assumptions

3. Box Plot Comparisons

  • Side-by-side box plots for completed vs. not completed groups
  • Shows distribution quartiles, medians, and outliers
  • Interactive hover information with individual data points

⚠️ Important Considerations

Sample Size Requirements: Statistical tests require at least 2 students per group. Results marked as NaN when insufficient data.
Multiple Testing: When testing multiple modules simultaneously, consider Bonferroni correction for p-values to control family-wise error rate.
Outlier Handling: Three modes available:
  • Include All Data: No outlier removal
  • Remove Statistical Outliers: IQR method (Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR)
  • Remove Grades < 20: Threshold method to exclude very low scores

🔍 Interpretation Guidelines

Statistical Significance

  • p < 0.001: Very strong evidence of difference
  • p < 0.01: Strong evidence of difference
  • p < 0.05: Moderate evidence of difference
  • p ≥ 0.05: No significant difference detected

Effect Size Considerations

  • Statistical significance ≠ practical significance
  • Consider mean difference magnitude in context
  • Sample size affects detection of small differences

Test Selection Logic

# From grade_module_correlation_helper.py lines 1360-1380 if shapiro_p1 >= 0.05 and shapiro_p2 >= 0.05: recommended_test = "Welch's t-test" recommendation_reason = "Both groups pass normality test" elif shapiro_p1 < 0.05 and shapiro_p2 < 0.05: recommended_test = "Mann-Whitney U" recommendation_reason = "Both groups fail normality test" else: recommended_test = "Mann-Whitney U" recommendation_reason = "Mixed normality results - using robust test"
